result.summary:
I recounted the two ABBA seals and the control independently. My own whitespace-token parser reads the raw logs in binary mode (scratch scripts in C:/kyty/s114/audit114/abba_recount/: parse_run.py, abba.py, admit.py, ctl_recount.py). I read the sealed scorers only for their definitions and imported no code from them. Rows are grouped by the emulator's own blk=/arm= fields, not by the scorers' frame formula. In both runs that grouping matches the formula block b = n 1801+90b..1890+90b for every complete block, and it matches the GateArm arm pattern 0,1,1,0 on all 197 GateArm lines. The row-level arm labels also check out: the first row of an arm-1 block already shows the arm-1 UpdateTitle wall (median 21 751 ns against 169 142 ns on the last arm-0 row). The logs I parsed are byte-identical to the scored inputs (log sha 77f0642a... for ttl114b, d721755d... for ttl114, as in the score JSONs).

Every number stated for seals 02b, 02 and 01 reproduces exactly (see recounts). Seal 02b is ADMITTED with S1 and S2 met, so SHIP stands. Seal 02 is NOT_ADMITTED, failing TITLE_ARMED alone. Seal 01 is PASS.

No BLOCKER and no MAJOR. Two MINOR findings:
- An unrelated single-thread 'find' process (pid 42220) kept about one of the 32 logical CPUs busy through ctl114, ttl114, ttl114b and vtt114b. The aggregate "CPU < 15 %" check cannot see this.
- ctl114.py's b_main_slept check takes the maximum over all MainTaskLate lines, not only those after the queued line. This has no effect in these runs.

Four INFO findings:
- P6 is empty: flip_rsv_wait_n is 0 on every row of both ABBA runs, although the counter is shown to work (ctl114a n=2973: 2 976 305 458 ns).
- Under the originally sealed 20 000 ns cap, ttl114b would also have failed admission. The verdict does not change for any cap from 22 234 ns up to, but not including, 172 556 ns, and the cap does not feed the estimator.
- The size is heavy-tailed: median pair d is -4.3 µs against a mean of -43.5 µs.
- The two ABBA runs are not independent at the pair level: per-pair d correlates 0.254 between them (fixed schedule on a deterministic scene).

findings.title: A background 'find' process kept one logical CPU busy through every deciding run (ctl114a/b, ttl114, ttl114b, vtt114b)
findings.evidence: The pre_run.host.top lists in the run metas show pid 42220 'find' with cpu_s 5865.1 (ctl114a.json, 01:42:17), 6071.3 (ctl114b.json, 01:45:44), 10720.8 (ttl114.json, 03:03:37), 18800.5 (ttl114b.json, 05:18:54) and 19436.3 (vtt114b.json, 05:29:32). CPU seconds per wall second: 206.2/207 = 0.996, 8079.7/8117 = 0.995, 635.8/638 = 0.997. So about one core ran continuously for more than 3.5 h, including during the 600-s ttl114b run itself. It is absent from vid114.json (06:14) and the boot metas, and it is no longer running. Pred 02 §2 says 'nothing else on the machine', and ROADMAP 114 item 6 requires 'no heavy processes'. The check actually applied was aggregate CPU < 15 %, but one of 32 logical CPUs is 3.1 %, which that check cannot see. go114c.sh has no CPU check, and the scorers read only pre-run GPU utilisation. The within-run ABBA pairing cancels a constant load to first order, so d and S1/S2 are not plausibly affected (S1 margin 93 µs). ctl114 is not affected either (3.03 s against 33 ms). Absolute levels and any cross-run comparison (e.g. vtt114b vs vid114) do carry it.
findings.fix: Record in FACTS/ROADMAP that seals 01, 02 and 02b and video vtt114b ran next to a one-core busy process. Add a per-process rate gate to enter_scene's pre-run: sample cpu_s twice about 10 s apart and refuse or wait if any non-system process uses more than 0.5 CPU s per wall s (the host.top data already holds cpu_s). Log the chain's own CPU check instead of doing it by hand.

findings.title: ctl114.py b_main_slept (and main_late_max_us) ignores where the MainTaskLate line sits
findings.evidence: C:/kyty/s114/ctl114.py:110-112 collects every MainTaskLate line in the log, and :136 and :162 use max(lates) with no after_queued filter. Pred 01 §4 is worded the same way, so the scorer is faithful to the seal. In these runs the other MainTaskLate lines are at startup (ctl114a line 4293: 232 158 µs; ctl114b line 4292: 208 599 µs). The deciding line in ctl114b is 3 000 429 µs at line 576458, after the queued line at 565529, so the verdict is unaffected. A long main-thread delay at startup (cold shader preparation, KYTY_PREPARE_HOLD_MS) of 2.5 s or more would satisfy the check without the stall.
findings.fix: In future controls, take only MainTaskLate lines after 'MainStallTest: queued' (and within the next ~5 s of rows), as a_waited_main already does by filtering on frame=3000.

findings.title: The quoted size is heavy-tailed, and the two ABBA runs share part of their pair structure
findings.evidence: ttl114b: per-pair d dt_us has median -4.3 against a mean of -43.5, a range from -833 to +834, and halves of -9.7 and -77.2. ttl114: median -3.7 against a mean of -51.6. Per-pair d correlates between the two runs at r = 0.254 (n = 96, p about 0.01). The same 67 ms game hitch falls at n=12280 in both runs, in block 116 (arm 0), and moves d by about -4 to -6 µs each time. With a fixed schedule on a deterministic scene, the same events land in the same arm, so 'a new independent run' replicates the noise but not that alignment. The effect on the decision is negligible given S1's margin.
findings.fix: Keep quoting the size as 'not distinguishable from zero' (as ROADMAP item 9 does). For replications, shift the schedule phase (e.g. start 1890 or BAAB) so scene-deterministic events change arm.

findings.title: The session-115 plan (item 13 (2)) is sound only if three conditions hold; two of them are deadlock traps
findings.evidence:
The presentation scheduler records in two spans: PrepareBlankFrame (producer==nullptr) at swapchain.cpp:815-818 and Present at swapchain.cpp:900-907. Both already run under the render mutex (swapchain.cpp:800 and :890), so those two spans are mutually exclusive today. The only thing that breaks is the owner claim at commandRecorder.cpp:323-326.

The swapchain section is not under any lock: AcquireNextImage (:877), swapchain.Present (:911), RecoverSwapchain (:881/:922). So C1, two threads presenting at once, needs its own exclusion.

Trap 1, the startup park: the park happens in UpdateTitle (:932 → window.cpp:791-794 waits for a drain). Only WindowContext::Run drains (window.cpp:852), and Run starts only after WindowPrepareShaders returns (emulator.cpp:187→197). A present mutex held across UpdateTitle would therefore deadlock every boot in which the main thread presents.

Trap 2, frame starvation: FramePool::Acquire and AcquireLast (swapchain.cpp:106-159) block until a frame is free. Frames are released only after UpdateTitle (:933), so waiting there while holding the mutex can starve.

The owner field is also read across threads: CommandRecorder::Drain reads m_producer from non-producer threads (commandRecorder.cpp:522), reached through DrainRecordQueues from every synchronous Submit (commandScheduler.cpp:199). m_producer is a plain std::thread::id (commandRecorder.h:300).

Count and log each handover so the boot check can prove it happened.

If C1 is also handled with a present mutex:
- Take it after FramePool::Acquire/AcquireLast.
- Release it before UpdateTitle, at the existing present_inside_guard.Leave() point.
- Keep the lock order cfg->mutex → present mutex → render mutex, and never take the present mutex while holding the render mutex.
